variants.headline: Business-start grant programme ends
variants.sub: Business-starting support under {programme} has come to an end.
variants.body:
The programme {programme} has ended, having paid {paid} grants and refused {refused} applications. It supported people starting a business. Readers considering {target} should distinguish that record from a judgment that either the existence or the end of a programme proves it served its purpose adequately.

The programme has ended. It leaves a count of grants paid and applications refused, not a tidy tale in which every ending explains itself. Readers can ask whether the support was worthwhile without turning a programme's closing notice into a made-up story about every person who applied.

The responsibility of {target} should be examined against the programme's recorded payments and refusals. Its conclusion is established, while the merits of individual outcomes require more than the fact of closure alone. Readers deserve a clear story and a straight answer about responsibility.

variants.headline: A grant scheme closes its account
variants.sub: The programme {programme} has ended its support for people starting a business.
variants.body:
